title: Minimax Matched-Pair Design with a Pilot-Estimated Prognostic Score
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4; not salvageable within scope. Math and decision panels pass; independent terminal-validity gate confirms sound below-floor contribution.
gap_reasons: The delivered equality concerns arbitrary pilot-dependent perfect matchings on the fixed regular-score-density class with L>1/2; regular-density-hypercube leaves the remaining nonempty radius regime unresolved, and the framing explicitly respects this restriction without a stale frontier overclaim. Relative to [Bai's Theorem 4.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.07845) and [Cytrynbaum's Theorems 3.4–3.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.18057v1), the additional result is the finite joint pilot-and-main converse under the score-density envelope, while oracle pairing, regression estimation, and geometric matching supply established upper-bound ingredients. The broad-anchor theorem establishes uniform pilot-insensitivity by permitting sample-size-dependent noise variance, so it contributes a nonuniformity extension and supplies no impossibility result under a common noise bound or a fixed law. The projected score is constrained by the restricted matching action, fixed known smoothness, unresolved radius coverage, and absence of calibrated finite-sample evidence translating the order-level pilot thresholds into usable variance or pilot-budget gains. The exhaustive four-unit calculations verify elementary identities but provide no evidence about the selector's practical performance across the three regimes. The proofless hilbert-holder-surjection lemma needs an explicit leaf citation to [Gerber–Chopin–Whiteley, Section 4.2.1 and Supplement S1.2](https://arxiv.org/html/1707.01845), whose public text supports the required classical fact; this is a citation repair, not a missing novel theorem. proof_attempt_summary: Derived the arbitrary-design joint pilot/main frontier on the regular-score-density class for L>1/2 and the broad finite-moment anchor geometric minimax rate; completed owned Lean proofs remain intact. The approved independent Uniform public-randomizer clarification, existing independent Bernoulli pilot-protocol synchronization, and exact Hilbert source attestation all passed current D0.5 math and decision reviews, but the typed novelty review capped the delivered package at subfield (7.3 below field threshold 7.4), confirmed by an independent terminal-validity consult. Intermediate-radius coverage and common-noise/fixed-law or broader-scope extensions require new research; preserve re-raise eligibility with a substantive extension.
tldr: A geometric-or-learned-score selector unconditionally attains \(\Phi_{m,N}=\min\{N^{-2\beta/d},N^{-2}+m^{-2\beta/(2\beta+d)}\}\) on the fixed regular-score-density class.  For \(L>1/2\), a folded-score construction proves the matching converse, so normalized minimax excess variance on that subclass is of order \(4\Phi_{m,N}\).  On the broader pilot-augmented radius-one Hölder anchor class, geometric matching is sharply minimax at pair-loss rate \(N^{-2\beta/d}\), equivalently normalized excess-variance rate \(4N^{-2\beta/d}\), for every pilot size: because only law-by-law finite second moments are imposed, least-favorable Gaussian noise can scale with \(m,N\) and keep the pilot uniformly uninformative.  Nonemptiness of the regular-score class requires \(L\geq(2d^{\beta/2})^{-1}\); the nonempty intermediate regime up to \(1/2\) remains unresolved.
gap: Bai2022Optimality proves oracle adjacent-score optimality and asymptotic equivalence for a consistent pilot score, but gives no finite joint pilot-and-main decision rate. Cytrynbaum2026Limits proves a no-pilot Hölder frontier using an atomic signed-tabletop family and does not permit pilot-informed matchings. The finite-pilot price under a common atomless score-density envelope is therefore not covered by either theorem.
fill: The selector upper bound combines a pilot regression guarantee, an exact pair-loss stability inequality with its cross term, an oracle spacing floor, and an all-dimensional geometric fallback. The converse conditions on the entire pilot and main covariates, converts unresolved local signs into posterior variance for singleton cells, and uses a folded scaffold to keep every score law inside the same density envelope.
